card.name: Words after under/by in older prose
card.fires_on: Small linking or modifying words (various, under, by, most, his, own, be) inside older literary or scientific prose, where the next word is a noun like heads, climates, or pupils.

modes.label: After under
modes.description: The word under or the word right after it, in phrases like 'under various heads' or 'under the most different climates'.
modes.example: arranged under<< various>> heads according to subject.

modes.label: Possessives and adverbs
modes.description: His, own, or an -ly ending in 19th-century essays, before a noun or description.
modes.example: risen above<< his>> own, can easily be imagined.

card.plain: It fires on small connecting words in old-fashioned essay prose, mostly in phrases like 'under various heads'.
